beats.t: Above, Yeoni held the thread. Below, the tail held the chain. Between them hung the black tiger.
Chairman. I'll write the ledger's last line myself.
What line?
Seo Hanbi. Repaid. One golden ring.
The tiger seized the ring around its neck with its right forepaw. Its claws sank into metal. The ring grew hot. Burning fur filled the air.
Let go. That ring is your body. Break it, and your power and road home break with it.
I know. That's why I'm breaking it.
Cracks split the ring. One, then two. Black smoke leaked through them. The tail screamed. The chain thrashed wildly.
The ring broke in two. The sound was small, like a single glass breaking. Yet that little sound reverberated through everything beneath the eclipse.
Black fur streamed away like rain. Claws shrank. The great body grew smaller. All that remained was a person in a wet coat.
Oh. It's colder than I expected.
She fell. Below, there was no chain left to catch her. Only a single red thread around her wrist.
Above, beside the well among the twenty-seven lunar mansions, the thread suddenly grew heavy. Yeoni pitched forward, knees striking stone.
Heavy! Heavier than before! Why?!
Not a tiger's weight. One person's weight. With no strength left to hold on.
Neo lowered his head to bite the thread. His foreleg passed straight through it. Transparent to the shoulder, it couldn't grasp anything.
Of all times to lose my strength. Damn it.
Move, cat! This is what aprons are for!
Moka untied his apron and knotted it around the thread. Yundal grabbed the end. The three lined up and pulled. Like tug-of-war, except their opponent was the universe.
One, two, three. I'm not normally the sort of person who does this.
Shut up and pull! Compatibility later!
A wet hand rose from the well. A ring-shaped scar circled its right wrist. Yeoni seized it. It was cold.
The person they hauled up lay coughing on the stone. Water streamed from her black coat. She clutched a soaked ledger.
My next-door neighbor.
Hello. Sorry to impose at this hour.
Yeoni was speechless. The neighbor who carried a black umbrella even on clear days. The voice nagging about socks through the wall. The name on the parcel label. All the same person.
You are imposing. A lot.
The rain stopped. Five sat around the well. Or rather, four and one. Seo Hanbi sat a little apart.
Almost no energy left. About one drop of water. Less than a hundredth of what you had as a tiger.
Very accurate. Are your readings always that precise?
Only with compatibility. Your birth date and time would improve the accuracy.
That's a debt.
You're pitching compatibility to her now?! She took every voice on our island!
Moka's whiskers trembled. His forepaws gripped his apron tightly. Seo Hanbi lifted her head and faced him without looking away.
Yes. I took them. The market grandmothers' voices. The children rapping on the underground stage. They're all in the ledger.
How can you say that so calmly?!
I'm pretending to be calm. Otherwise I can't get the words out.
Moka closed his mouth. He didn't look any less angry. But he stopped shouting.
Seo Hanbi opened the ledger. Names crowded the wet pages. Yeoni's name stood among them. In the next column: Outstanding. Outstanding.
I'll start with the excuse. Otherwise what comes afterward won't be honest.
Go ahead.
That spring, I was deceived. Black Moon came wearing your face and took my envelope. I believed you'd abandoned me.
So I said I'd stop you before you became a monster. I wore the ring as the price. Up to that point, Black Moon was to blame.
Seo Hanbi paused. Her finger rubbed the ledger's corner, raising the paper's fibers.
But although Black Moon deceived me, the hand that stole the child's applause was mine.
When the drummer child cried, I wrote: Collection complete. On Moka's island, on the island of time too. I did it all with my own hands.
No one spoke. Only water dripped at the bottom of the well. Drip. Drip.
Thank you. For saving me earlier. And for not making excuses now.
Yes.
But I don't forgive you. Not now.
Yeoni's voice shook. Even they couldn't tell whether it was anger or tears. Still, they finished.
That drummer child really cried that day. I saw it. So did the grandmothers on Moka's island. You haven't returned anything to them. I can't forgive you ahead of them.
For now, I'll only say thank you. Forgiveness comes later. I decide that too.
That's right. If I were forgiven now, my ledger wouldn't balance either.
The ledger again.
A habit. I'll work on it. Slowly.
Seo Hanbi turned the ledger's pages again and placed a finger on one voice in the collection column. She tried to push the letters backward. The ink wouldn't move.
Ah. I paid away the power to return things too. As part of the ring's price.
What tiger power collected can only be released by tiger power. You can't do it in this body.
Then I'll have to find another way. Even if it takes time.
Do it, however long it takes. The grandmothers are waiting.
Moka said only that and turned away. But he didn't leave. He pushed his remaining box of matches toward Seo Hanbi, as though telling her to dry her coat.
May I take these? What do I owe?
Owe, my tail. Just use them. Sharing fire doesn't make it smaller.
Night came. The twenty-seven moons lit one by one. Yeoni sat on the well's edge and took out their notebook. Neo lay down beside them.
Seo Hanbi. Rescued. Forgiveness pending. Drummer child's name: still unknown.
Yeoni's pen stopped. The scene that had traveled up the thread remained in their mind. The rainy bus stop. The man who dropped his white umbrella.
Neo. Were you at that bus stop too?
What bus stop?
The white umbrella. 'Too late. Again.' That voice was yours.
Neo's hand went still. Instead of answering, he looked down at his arm. It was transparent to the shoulder.
There are things I can't say. Not simply because I want to hide them.
That again? Everyone has too many secrets. Does this world's customer support not have a notices page?
It does. Nobody reads it.
Don't be funny. None of this is funny.
Yeoni looked at Neo's transparent foreleg. They reached to touch it, then stopped. It seemed even more frightening to feel their hand pass through.
Then answer just one thing. That spring too—were you on my side?
That I can say. I'm on your side. From the beginning to now.
(Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. I have to preserve that much.)
Yeoni pressed the words into a corner of the notebook. Neo pretended not to see.
Across the well, Seo Hanbi counted moons alone. Neo walked over silently and stood beside her.
You were the one who arrived late then. The white umbrella.
Yes. And you were still there.
Neither of us protected her.
This time will be different. For you too.
I have no power now. I can't wield light the way you can.
It's hard for me to wield it now too. This arm is disappearing first.
Seo Hanbi looked down at Neo's leg. For the first time, her unsmiling face tightened.
Does she know?
No. She mustn't. Don't tell her either.
You're putting me in your debt.
Yes. Repay me later.
At dawn, one of the twenty-seven moons abruptly went dark. Yeoni's moon, Bharani. A round patch blackened in the sky.
Oh. That's strange. I feel hollow again.
An enormous head descended from the black circle. A head without a body: Rahu. Each time its mouth opened, starlight was sucked inside.
The head eats the future. My lady, your notebook!
Yeoni opened it. Next week's to-do list was disappearing line by line. Grocery shopping. Submit assignment. Go to the sea. The words turned into black smoke and rose into the sky.
Why the sea?! We haven't even picked a date!
Promises without dates taste best. Like the promise you two once failed to keep.
Seo Hanbi went pale. Only the two of them knew that promise. And the thing that had slipped between them.
[ Year: Im-o · Frozen ] Cracks spreading
I have no use for a dog without a collar. I shall empty you along with that vessel.
The head descended. Yeoni stepped back. Neo moved forward, but his legs couldn't find purchase on the floor.
What stepped in front of them was a wet coat. Seo Hanbi, unarmed, without claws or fangs.
What are you doing? You said you have no power!
I don't. But this time I won't walk toward that side.
I don't even have an umbrella. Let alone half of one.
Rahu's mouth opened. Then something fell onto Seo Hanbi's palm. A single cold drop. Clear, not black.
...Rain?
